user.title: Watt Window
user.description: Finds the cheapest time to use electricity, using Nord Pool prices, your tariff and (optionally) a Forecast.Solar forecast.

data_description.preset: A starting point. You can adjust every rate on the next screen.
data_description.country: Two-letter code, e.g. EE, GB. Holidays count as night on day/night tariffs. Leave empty to ignore holidays.

tariff.title: Your tariff
tariff.description: All rates per kWh, before VAT, in your Nord Pool currency.

data.margin: Supplier margin on top of spot

data_description.other_per_kwh: Taxes and fees charged per kWh, e.g. renewable fee, excise, balancing charge.

solar_menu.title: Solar panels
solar_menu.description: Should Watt Windows take your solar panels into account? You can change this, and add detail, later on Watt Window's Settings tab.

menu_options.estimate: Yes, estimate it for me (free, from Open-Meteo)

solar.title: Solar forecast
solar.description: Pick your Forecast.Solar setup. If you tick more than one, their forecasts are added up.

data.base_load_w: What your house uses on its own
data.can_export: My system sends spare power to the grid

data_description.base_load_w: Your panels power the house first; only what's left over makes a Watt Window cheaper. If you don't know, leave 500 W. You can read the real figure from your energy dashboard at night, when nothing big is running.
data_description.can_export: Leave on if you're paid for (or can send) power you don't use. Turn off if your inverter holds the panels back instead ("zero export"): then spare solar is simply lost, so using it is free.

battery_menu.title: Home battery
battery_menu.description: Do you have a home battery? This is saved but doesn't change anything yet: battery-aware Watt Windows (storing spare solar for later) come in a later version.

menu_options.battery: Yes, I have a home battery

estimate.title: Your panels
estimate.description: One rough number is enough to start. Watt Window assumes a south-facing roof at 35° until you tell it more: add each roof plane's tilt and direction later on the Settings tab if you know them.

data.base_load_w: What your house uses on its own
data.can_export: My system sends spare power to the grid

data_description.kwp: The kWp on your installation paperwork or inverter app. A guess is fine: e.g. 12 panels of 400 W = 4.8 kWp.
data_description.base_load_w: Your panels power the house first; only what's left over makes a Watt Window cheaper. If you don't know, leave 500 W.
data_description.can_export: Leave on if you're paid for (or can send) power you don't use. Turn off if your inverter holds the panels back instead ("zero export"): then spare solar is simply lost, so using it is free.

abort.no_nordpool: Set up the Nord Pool integration first (Settings > Devices & services > Add integration > Nord Pool).
abort.single_instance_allowed: Watt Window is already set up.

error.bad_rate: Every network rate needs a number.
error.bad_hours: The day rate must start before it ends, between 0 and 24.
error.bad_day_hours: The day must start before it ends, between 0 and 24.
error.bad_solar: That Forecast.Solar setup no longer exists.
error.bad_planes: Each roof plane needs a size above 0 kWp and a tilt between 0 and 90°.
